<BEGIN_SHACL>
@prefix sh:   <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#> .
@prefix vocab: <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#> .
@prefix xsd:   <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> .
@prefix ex:    <http://example.org/shacl#> .

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Shape that captures the welding requirement for weld entities.
# It is **not** a target shape; it is only invoked from the ship shape
# via the hasWeld property (see ex:ShipShape below).  This respects the
# admission boundary which declares the population owner class as
# https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#ship.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
ex:WeldRequirementShape
    a sh:NodeShape ;
    ## Requirement: if a weld is within an ice‑strengthened area,
    ## then its weld type must be the double continuous weld.
    ## Expressed as: ( NOT withinIceStrengthenedArea ) OR ( weldType = doubleContinuousWeld )
    sh:or (
        # Case 1 – the weld is **not** within an ice‑strengthened area.
        [
            sh:property [
                sh:path vocab:withinIceStrengthenedArea ;
                sh:hasValue false ;
                sh:datatype xsd:boolean ;
                sh:message "Weld is not within an ice‑strengthened area." ;
            ] ;
        ]
        # Case 2 – the weld is within an ice‑strengthened area and must be double‑continuous.
        [
            sh:property [
                sh:path vocab:weldType ;
                sh:hasValue vocab:doubleContinuousWeld ;
                sh:nodeKind sh:IRI ;
                sh:message "Weld within ice‑strengthened area must be of type double continuous." ;
            ] ;
        ]
    ) ;
    sh:message "Weld does not satisfy the double‑continuous requirement for ice‑strengthened areas." .

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Ship shape that links ships to their welds and enforces the weld
# requirement on each associated weld.
# The target class is exactly the declared owner class, satisfying the
# admission scope constraint.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
ex:ShipShape
    a sh:NodeShape ;
    sh:targetClass vocab:ship ;
    sh:property [
        sh:path vocab:hasWeld ;
        sh:node ex:WeldRequirementShape ;
        sh:message "Associated weld must satisfy the double‑continuous requirement when positioned in ice‑strengthened areas." ;
    ] ;
    sh:message "Ship has welds that violate the double‑continuous welding rule for ice‑strengthened areas." .
<END_SHACL>

We need to revise previous SHACL to fix ADMISSION_SCOPE_ERROR: "Other target classes select beyond declared population". The declared owner_class is https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#ship. The SHACL currently has two shapes:

- ex:WeldRequirementShape targetClass vocab:weld (fine)
- ex:ShipShape targetClass vocab:ship (fine)

But perhaps the issue is that the weld shape is also a target class, but the admission limit says only target class ship is allowed (owner_class). The admission policy likely restricts shapes to target only the owner_class (ship) because the population boundary is ship class. So we need to constrain activation to that boundary: i.e., only evaluate weld requirement via nested property path from ship, not via own targetClass.

Therefore we should remove sh:targetClass vocab:weld from the weld shape; instead, make it a sh:property shape applied via ship shape's property. The ship shape already references ex:WeldRequirementShape as node for hasWeld. That's fine. So remove targetClass from weld shape (or replace with sh:targetNode? but we must not target beyond ship). So modify weld shape: remove sh:targetClass vocab:weld. Possibly add sh:node ex:WeldRequirementShape as a shape that is applied via property, not requiring its own target.

Thus revised SHACL: ex:WeldRequirementShape a sh:NodeShape ; sh:property ...? Actually we need shape for weld nodes but not a target; can be used as node shape in property constraint.

So final SHACL should have ex:WeldRequirementShape with sh:property constructs that reference weld's own properties but not targetClass.

We must preserve obligations, paths etc. Keep everything else.

Thus produce block with <BEGIN_SHACL> ... <END_SHACL>.
